issues: Cancel triggers no confirm dialog; a one-tap destructive cancel is a mild UX risk (single click removes an active paid sponsorship). Consider a Confirm-cancel modal or optimistic undo.

critical_code_review_comments: routes/social_v2.py:_owned_merchant_or_403 correctly resolves both business_id and _id and both owner_user_id/owner_user_ids — good defensive impl.

routes/social_v2.py:rail_sponsor_checkout falls back to instant-activate on ANY Stripe exception (broad `except Exception`). In production this masks real Stripe outages behind free activation. For preview/test this is acceptable, but a live guard (env STRIPE_MODE=='live' → do not auto-activate) would prevent free comping. Recommend narrowing to `except stripe.error.*` and only auto-activating when STRIPE_MODE!='live'.

routes/social_v2.py:rail_event does not authenticate the sponsorship_id against the current user — any authenticated user can inflate a merchant's impressions/clicks by POSTing forged events. Consider validating that the sponsorship exists and is active before counting it, or at least dedup by (user_id, sponsorship_id, action, minute-bucket) to prevent trivial CTR gaming.
MerchantRailSponsor.jsx:cancel() shows no confirmation and immediately calls the API — see design_issues above.

MerchantRailSponsor.jsx error toast only maps 'not_your_business'; other codes ('wrong_status','bad_tier','show_not_found_or_not_host') fall through to a generic error. Consider mapping them for clearer merchant feedback.
